problem: Mandrel sizes are normally quoted as diameter, so a 10 mm mandrel means a 5 mm bend radius. The next sentence says a 5 mm radius can already cost noticeable loss, which contradicts the harmless 10 mm check. A student cannot tell whether 10 mm is the diameter or the radius.
fix: Write the units clearly: 'wraps a few turns around a 10 mm diameter mandrel, which gives a 5 mm bend radius' and then say which of 5 mm or 10 mm bend radius is the harmless case.

problem: The sentence 'It is not a loss per kilometre' contradicts the comparison table in Section 2, which gives micro bending in dB/km. The student sees one statement saying bend loss is never per km and another giving it per km.
fix: Say 'Macro bend loss is quoted as dB per turn at a stated radius and wavelength, not as dB per kilometre. Micro bending, being spread along the whole length, is quoted in dB/km.'

problem: The text says the real curve is flat at large R and turns up sharply near R_c, but the plot draws one exponential 8e^(−0.6R) over the whole 2–12 mm range, which keeps falling steeply and never flattens or kinks. A student may take the exponential as the true physical curve at all radii.
fix: Add a line under the figure: 'This is the measured fit A e^(−BR) over the tested range only; outside that range the real curve flattens at large R and rises sharply near R_c.'
